methodology.how: *** THE TO LEFT write_paths AS 'UNMEASURED -- yours to resolve'. RESOLVED: ONE WRITE PATH, TWO TABLES. NOT a path-multiplicity surprise. *** All four Iceberg write operations in this 3174-line module live inside a SINGLE function, cmd_iceberg_commit() (:2964-3101): create_table for nodes (:3034), create_table for edges (:3047), nodes_table.overwrite (:3051), edges_table.overwrite (:3091). They share one invocation, one mechanism (full-table overwrite), one authority and one trigger, which is the same shape the decomp already treats as ONE path in derive_runner PATH A (graph_nodes + graph_edges through one helper). Mechanically: namespace create (:3013, exception-swallowed), then load-or-create each table against a locally-declared Schema (:3021-3037 nodes, :3038-3048 edges), then overwrite each from a pa.table built by list comprehension over all_nodes/all_edges. The edges branch runs an endpoint-resolution guard FIRST (:3072-3089) and REFUSES the overwrite with RC_FAIL if any edge has an empty endpoint.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: EDGES: fails closed since the A11 fix. The endpoint resolver _nid tries 'source'/'src' then 'target'/'dst' (:3072-3080); any edge resolving to an empty endpoint triggers a refusal -- prints the offender, prints 'REFUSING to overwrite globgrph.graph_edges', returns RC_FAIL (:3081-3089). NODES: NO equivalent guard. The nodes branch (:3049-3060) overwrites unconditionally on a truthy all_nodes, with n.get('id','') defaulting to the empty string per row. NAMESPACE: create_namespace failure is swallowed by a bare `except Exception: pass` (:3013-3015).
silent_degrade_paths: *** THE HISTORICAL DEFECT, RECORDED AT THE SITE (:3062-3071, CVO 2026-07-10): *** this function read e['src']/e['dst'] while both edges.append sites in the module emit {'source','target'}, so _nid returned '' for EVERY edge and graph_edges was overwritten with empty src_id/dst_id on all rows. It was SILENT precisely because the schema's required=True is satisfied by ''. The remedy landed and IS the :3081-3089 guard -- so the edges arm is now loud. I am recording it because it is the clearest measured instance in this wave of a NOT-NULL constraint failing to be an IS-MEANINGFUL constraint.

The nodes arm still carries the shape the edges arm was fixed for: n.get('id', '') at :3052 defaults to '' and no guard rejects it, so a node list with unresolvable ids overwrites graph_nodes with empty node_id rows and returns RC_OK. The asymmetry is measured, not alleged: the guard exists at :3081-3089 for edges and has no counterpart before :3051. NAMED, NOT FIXED (CCX3-AC8) -- and note this verb is recommended for deprecation, so the correct remedy may be removal rather than a second guard. That call is not this seat's.
`except Exception: pass` on create_namespace (:3013-3015) converts an instrument failure into a verdict -- a permissions or connectivity fault reads identically to 'namespace already exists'.

Both overwrites are full-table replaces with no filter, and this module's declared schemas are NARROWER than derive_runner's for the same tables (no 'source', no 'props'). An invocation of this verb after a nightly can therefore REMOVE columns the nightly writes -- last-writer-wins on shape, not merely on rows.

verdict.why: All seven rows measured against source at 3b918f21b42366fce14f7c2076f18444cd782931 and against both live trigger planes. The TO's UNMEASURED write-path question is RESOLVED: ONE write path, two tables, one function, one mechanism -- NOT a BLOCKING path-multiplicity surprise, and the measurement (AST enclosure test over all four write linenos) is stated so it can be re-run. QUALIFIED, not SOUND, on four named defects, none of which blocks USE of this card: (1) the nodes arm has no endpoint guard and will overwrite graph_nodes with empty node_id rows at RC_OK -- the same shape the edges arm was repaired for; (2) this module's declared schemas for graph_nodes/graph_edges are narrower than derive_runner's for the SAME tables, and both writers full-overwrite, so shape is last-writer-wins; (3) a bare `except Exception: pass` on namespace creation turns instrument failure into a verdict; (4) no denominator -- this verb has no observed run to count. It is NOT UNSOUND: the verb is untriggered on both planes and has no executable caller, so the nodes-arm defect is latent rather than firing nightly. It would become UNSOUND the moment anything scheduled it.
